utility.notes: BWL is a municipally-owned utility (not an investor-owned utility like DTE or Consumers Energy) serving the City of Lansing directly — a genuinely different ownership structure worth noting alongside DTE Energy's territory researched separately this session (see mi-washtenaw-annarbor-dte).

value.name: Lansing Board of Water & Light (BWL)
value.notes: BWL is a municipally-owned utility that is itself the generation and distribution utility for Lansing; no separate generation supplier or CCA applies.

permit_authority.value: City of Lansing Building Safety Office (Economic Development & Planning)
permit_authority.notes: Michigan's statewide Residential Code sets the baseline, but enforcement is delegated to whichever local jurisdiction has assumed local-enforcing-agency status (see the identical statewide structural note on the Ann Arbor, MI record, mi-washtenaw-annarbor-dte). Lansing's own Building Safety Office is the local AHJ; applications are processed through the City's BS&A Online portal. A dedicated solar-specific permitting checklist was not located and confirmed this session — this authority/process information reflects the City's general building-permit process page.

interconnection_url.notes: Per BWL's own page, customers must contact BWL's distributed generation team before purchasing equipment. Before construction, the contractor must submit an Interconnection Application and comply with BWL's Rules and Regulations; an interconnection fee applies (specific dollar amount not stated on the page fetched this session). BWL compensates excess exported solar energy at a 'Solar Outflow Credit' of $0.075/kWh, itself composed of an energy cost average ($0.050/kWh), a capacity credit ($0.012/kWh), and a renewable energy credit ($0.013/kWh) — a distinct rate-design approach from DTE's Rider 18 program.

value.name: Building Permit Application or Application for Plan Review, plus construction documents and the required fee

required_documents.notes: This is the City's general building-permit application requirement; a dedicated solar-specific document checklist was not located this session. Separately, BWL's own rebate application requires: a signed rebate application, invoice/proof of purchase, installation date, and equipment specification sheets.

value: Applicant contacts BWL with a request for information; BWL provides the 'Generator Interconnection Application'
BWL receives the Interconnection Application, supporting data, and a $100 interconnection application fee
BWL acknowledges receipt within 5 business days
BWL reviews the application data and confirms the inverter meets IEEE Std. 1547 requirements
If approved, the project design is approved for construction; the customer must also have applied for a City of Lansing electrical permit
BWL and the local Electrical Inspector approve the completed installation
BWL and the customer execute the Generator Interconnection Agreement and contract for parallel operation, and BWL provides Net Metering program information/application
inspection_steps.notes: Per BWL's own 'BWL Interconnection Process' flowchart document, specifically scoped to 'Customer Owned Renewable Energy Generators Inverter-Type Projects 20kW or Less' — i.e. the residential-scale process, not BWL's separate large-generator/transmission-level interconnection procedure (BWL Procedural Guideline PG-02-0002), which was also reviewed this session but found to be out of scope for a typical residential rooftop system. The $100 fee shown here is a BWL utility interconnection fee, not a City of Lansing building-permit fee — see permit_fees for the (unconfirmed) City fee.

timeline_days.notes: No City permit review timeline was confirmed this session. BWL's own page states rebate application processing takes up to 4 weeks — a utility-rebate timeline, not the building-permit timeline.

other_conditions: BWL's own page recommends contacting the utility's distributed generation team before purchasing equipment to discuss appropriate system sizing

permit_fees.notes: No specific City building-permit fee figure was confirmed this session. BWL's own page confirms an interconnection fee applies to the utility application but does not state the dollar amount on the page fetched — left null rather than estimated.

value.name: BWL Solar Rebate
value.description: Rebate for customer-owned residential solar systems. Required documentation: signed rebate application, invoice/proof of purchase, installation date, and equipment specification sheets; processing takes up to 4 weeks.
value.eligibility: Capped at $2,000 total, corresponding to a 4kW system at the $500/kW rate
